newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt says jumbo broadcasting amendment ready.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt says jumbo broadcasting amendment ready.

text.p: The Italian government has drafted an umbrella amendment to unify three decrees on broadcasting which should be approved before Christmas, Posts and Telecoms Ministry undersecretary Vincenzo Vita said.
"The measure is ready and must be approved by Christmas," Vita told Reuters by telephone.

The decrees include one which would extend broadcasting licences due to expire at the end of January, which mainly concerns former prime minister and centre-right leader Silvio Berlusconi's Mediaset television group.
All three decrees were due to expire before Christmas.

The umbrella amendment is the result of an initial accord reached earlier this week between the centre-left government and the centre-right opposition to extend the January expiry of licences to the end of May 1997.

A December 1994 ruling said no single proprietor should be allowed to keep three channels and the government has presented a bill to shake up the sector but this has been held up by disagreement over a part of the bill concerning the telecommunications sector.
